about: Team tooling incidents, one record per root cause. Evidence kinds: commit (sha on main), event (seq in .fw-console/events.jsonl, local-only), ci (GitHub Actions run id), file (repo path), proc (process shape, no pids that matter later). Each incident names the work-graph task that fixes it (fix.task, plus fix.also); status is derived, never stored: fixed iff fix.task and every also task are done, fixing iff one of them is claimed, else open (Fw.Plan.Incident; check with pnpm fw incidents lint, see README.md). Each incident also carries its mistake-retro link (research/mistakes/ledger.json): leanVerdict (provable | partly | no), leanReason, hardening (a work-graph task id; required unless the verdict is no), empiricalCheck (the test or CI check; required when the verdict is no), mistakeClass (a retro class id) and mistake (the retro row, informational).

incidents.title: The lead started fw watch with a trailing & inside a foreground shell call, four times; the watcher outlived the call as an orphan (a fifth launch was chained in a background call)
incidents.symptom: A `pnpm fw watch ... &` launched inside a foreground Bash call kept running after the call returned, with no owner the harness tracks and no end notification; the lead found it later and killed it by its own PID. It was the second launch in the same form. It came back a third time (fw watch --until-alert &) and a fourth time within the hour (`pnpm fw watch ... & disown` chained onto a work-graph commit command), both after wait-guard had landed in shadow mode; each orphan was killed by its own PID. A fifth launch (batch 4) chained `pnpm fw watch` after `gh run cancel` inside one run_in_background call: not an orphan, because the harness owned the call, but it broke the rule that fw watch runs alone in its own background call.
incidents.cause: INFERRED (lead's mistake list; harness behaviour of `&` in a foreground call): a trailing `&` detaches the child from the tool call, so nothing holds a handle, a bound or an end signal for it. The sanctioned forms (run_in_background, or a monitor with an until predicate) are prose rules; nothing refuses a long-runner launched with `&`. The third and fourth launches show the habit of chaining the relaunch onto the previous command; memory and a logged incident did not stop it, and wait-guard in shadow mode (b42769d) only logs.
